posts.text: This is very subjective question and everbody has its own perspective on it. What I feel is that I don’t need to sell because the business has become bad; I sell when the expected return from the current price no longer compensates me adequately for the risks and assumptions involved. In simple terms, margin of safety is not about buying a good company cheaply—it is about making sure I can still be reasonably right even if my assumptions turn out to be somewhat wrong. Hopefully I answered your query. I dont consider myself subject expert on this topic. Just my 2 cents. I may be wrong so take m…
